sources.title: Government of The Gambia: Immigration and visa information
sources.officialityEvidence: The Government of The Gambia publishes this entry guidance on gambia.gov.gm. The page identifies its 3 January 2025 publication date and states the visitor waiver categories and Banjul airport contingency.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the United Kingdom, full members of the European Union, the Commonwealth [and] ECOWAS do not require a visa.

sources.title: Gambia Immigration Department: Entry requirements
sources.officialityEvidence: The Government directory identifies gid.gov.gm as Gambia Immigration Department’s official site. Its current entry-requirements page describes ECOWAS entry, visas at gazetted ports, clearance, screening and arrival requirements.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa for entry ... can be obtained ... from Immigration officers at the various gazetted port of entries.

sources.title: Gambia Immigration Department: Visa guidance and country table
sources.officialityEvidence: GID publishes this live visa page on its official gid.gov.gm domain. Its WordPress API reports a 31 October 2025 modification and it gives country headings for visa-and-clearance, visa-only and clearance-only groups, warning that statuses can change.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The statuses of various countries above are subjected to changes due to circumstances.

sources.title: Government of The Gambia: Passport Office and citizen return
sources.officialityEvidence: The Government Passport Office page cites Immigration Act Cap. 16:02 sections 4A and 4B, identifies ordinary, service and diplomatic passport categories, and describes emergency passport return for Gambian citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: the Gambia diplomatic or consular service ... shall issue him or her Emergency Passport to travel back to the Gambia.

sources.title: ECOWAS Information System: current Member States
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The ECOWAS Information System is on the official ecois.ecowas.int domain and currently enumerates 12 Member States, including The Gambia and the mapped 11 foreign passport states.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ECOWAS Information System ... 12 ECOWAS Member States.

sources.title: EUR-Lex: Member States of the European Union
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex is the EU’s official law portal. Its current Member States page lists all 27 members and notes that the United Kingdom withdrew in 2020.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Now there are 27 Member States: Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia ... Sweden.

policies.title: Gambian ordinary passports: citizenship
policies.summary: Gambian citizenship, rather than a visitor visa category, governs the home-country entry classification. The Government Passport Office page directly describes a Gambian citizen receiving an emergency passport to travel back to The Gambia.
conditions: This is a citizenship normalization for a Gambian ordinary passport, not a rule for residence, former citizenship, nationality disputes, emergency, diplomatic, service or other special documents.

The cited Passport Office material describes return by an emergency passport after loss or destitution. Passport validity, identity, security, health, border examination and other lawful controls remain applicable.

policies.title: Current GID-listed and reconciled ordinary passports: visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The current GID table expressly lists 17 catalog passports with visa-exemption agreements and 11 ECOWAS states with free entry. The January 2025 central Government page additionally supports Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia, which the newer GID table does not classify. This yields 32 supported foreign catalog passports; its conflicting visa/clearance rows do not establish a further route.
conditions: The GID page’s dated country entries support the 17 agreement-listed catalog codes and 11 current ECOWAS codes. Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia are retained only because the central Government page expressly places all EU members in its waiver category and GID gives none of those four a contrary country row.

The waiver is modelled for ordinary nationality passports only. It does not establish British Overseas Territories, Crown Dependencies, Hong Kong, Macao, refugee, stateless, emergency, diplomatic, official, service, UN, residence or other special-document treatment.

The GID exemption and ECOWAS rows do not publish an exemption-stay period. The January 2025 central Government page describes the waiver visitor context as holiday or business not exceeding 90 days; duration, passport validity, yellow-fever evidence where applicable, screening, funds/onward travel, security and final admission remain subject to GID control.

The current GID table (modified 31 October 2025) puts many other EU or Commonwealth passports in visa and/or clearance groups, while the central page says the broad categories are exempt. Those incompatible scopes are deliberately unresolved; a clearance label is not normalized as visa on arrival, eVisa or a nationality-wide advance-visa rule.
